target: /pages/our-philosophy — centre the standards section's header, leaving the two columns left-aligned
note:
Malcolm: 'Center align the first text block.' That is the section header — subheading, heading and intro paragraph — and NOT the two standards columns, whose body copy stays left-aligned because centred four-line paragraphs read badly.

WHY THIS NEEDS CSS AND NOT THE SETTING. `multi-column` has one `text_alignment` setting and it drives BOTH halves: the snippet is rendered with `text_alignment: section.settings.text_alignment`, and the same value is emitted onto every block as a `justify-<value>` class. Setting it to `center` would centre the columns too and then need CSS to undo that — two rules and a fight with the setting. Leaving it at `start` and centring only the header is one rule.

MEASURED, NOT GUESSED. `section-header` is a GRID whose track is `grid-template-columns: 700px` with `justify-content: start`, sitting in a 1344px container at a 1440 viewport — so the heading is a 700px column pinned left, and `text-align` alone would not move it. Centring the TRACK is what is required, which is `justify-content`. At 390 the track measures 350px against a 350px container, so the same rule is a no-op there and mobile is unaffected.

SCOPING. This style section lives in `templates/page.philosophy.json`, so it only loads on this page, and the page carries exactly one `multi-column` (measured live). The class is therefore sufficient and, unlike a `shopify-section-template--<theme id>__standards` id selector, it does not go stale when the theme is duplicated. Section ids were not an option for that reason.

APPENDED AT THE END OF THE TEMPLATE, after `cta`. ADR-006 warns that a `custom-html` section dropped mid-order silently collapses the FOLLOWING section's padding — a zero-height section is not zero-effect. Placing it last means there is no following section for it to collapse, which is why every style section on `templates/index.json` sits at the end. `remove_vertical_spacing` and `remove_horizontal_spacing` are both true so the wrapper itself contributes no height.

No Liquid tags and no `{{` anywhere in the CSS, including inside the comments — `custom-html` rejects double braces with a 422 whose real message is buried in the response body, and Liquid parses the contents of a CSS comment too.

settings.html:
<style>
  /* /pages/our-philosophy — centre the standards section's header only.

     section-header is a grid with a fixed 700px track and justify-content:
     start, so the heading sits as a 700px column pinned to the left of a
     1344px container. text-align on its own moves the text inside the track
     but not the track itself, so the block would still read left. Centring
     the TRACK is the actual fix; justify-items and text-align then centre
     the subheading, heading and intro within it.

     At 390 the track is 350px in a 350px container, so this is a no-op on
     mobile and nothing there changes.

     Scoped by class rather than by section id: this style section lives in
     the philosophy template so it loads on no other page, and the page holds
     exactly one multi-column. A template--<theme id>__standards selector goes
     stale the moment the theme is duplicated. */
  .shopify-section--multi-column section-header {
    justify-content: center;
    justify-items: center;
    text-align: center;
  }

  /* The two standards columns stay LEFT. They already do, because the section
     setting is start — this is a guard, so that if the alignment setting is
     ever flipped in the theme editor to centre the header the hard way, the
     body copy does not silently become centred with it. */
  .shopify-section--multi-column .multi-column__item {
    text-align: start;
  }
</style>
